Learning path

Seven levels, from simple to complex

Check it yourself

Put in your own order, delivery and invoice

One line of one invoice, or load one of the levels above. The page compares price and quantity, applies your tolerance, and splits the invoice into the part to pay and the part to dispute. Nothing is sent anywhere.

From the purchase order
From the goods receipt
From the invoice
Your tolerance policy (leave blank for exact match)

The split follows the skill's Step 5: pay the matched portion, dispute the remainder. "Matched portion" here means the smaller of received and billed quantity, at the agreed price. The skill's default with no tolerance is exact match — any difference is an exception. The fifteen exception types and their severities are the skill's own rules, not a published standard.

Rules are the skill's own. Facts below come from procurement regulation, the US internal-control standard, the fraud examiners' association, an accounting standard-setter and the accounting software's own documentation, as published when checked on 21 October 2026 — follow the link for today's wording.

    Not backed by an outside authority: the fifteen exception types and their severities, the exact-match default, and the matching precedence (line number, then SKU, then description) are the skill's own rules. The page marks them as the skill's where they appear.

    Using it

    What it asks, needs and gives back

    Asks firstMosofin or upload? Your tolerance? Who may approve what? Services in scope, and what stands in for a receipt? Foreign-currency policy? Who owns exceptions?
    NeedsThe invoices — always in the books; purchase orders where the system holds them; delivery records, which it usually has to ask for.
    Gives backPay / Hold / Reject per invoice, every line side by side with its match basis, every exception with an owner, the tests that could not run, and the month's patterns.
    NeverPays, holds or releases money; invents a tolerance; lets an untested check read as a pass; concludes fraud. It reads nothing before you say yes.
    Rules are quoted from the skill's own file, SKILL.md — the opening section on which legs exist, Steps 2–5, the exception table and the Edge Cases. Facts are cited to the sources above.
